newsitem.title: ITALY: Canada ready to lead Zaire force-Boutros.
newsitem.headline: Canada ready to lead Zaire force-Boutros.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali confirmed on Tuesday that Canada was ready to command a multinational force in Zaire and said he hoped it would have logistical support from the United States.

The U.N. chief also said that South Africa had agreed in principle to take part. "I hope in the next few days we will be able to have these multinational forces and we will have a mandate from the Security Council," he told a news conference.
Boutros-Ghali, in Rome for a world food summit, said he had spoken about the humanitarian crisis in Zaire with Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Monday.
"I express my gratitude to Canada. Canada has accepted to command these multinational forces...Canada is a very neutral country," he said.

"This morning I was able to have direct contact with Nelson Mandela and he agreed in principle that South Africa will participate in multinational forces," Boutros-Ghali said, adding Italy had made a similar commitment in principle.

"We are in contact with Canada, Italy, France, Spain, and we hope also to have logistical support from the United States." He said the size of a force had not been set but added: "People are talking of between 10,000 and 12,000 with the cost shared by member states who are participating."
